criteria.true: Announces an event worth knowing about

announces_event.instructions: Does `email` announce an event, gathering, meeting, or date-bound occasion the recipient might want to attend or be aware of — a church event, concert, webinar, meetup, appointment window? Check against `email.dates_mentioned`: a bare date with no event attached (copyright notice, '30-day guarantee') does not count.

is_compound.instructions: Does `email` contain more than one distinct topic or request — e.g. a newsletter that also asks for a reply, or an FYI bundled with an action item? A single focused message is not compound.

is_scam.instructions: Is `email` a scam, phishing attempt, or unsolicited spam?

is_stale.instructions: Has the usefulness of `email` already passed (expired sale, used one-time code, past event, delivered package)? Use `email.received` and `email.dates_mentioned`.

company_automated.covers: Sent by a system: marketing blasts, order/shipping notices, TOS updates, feature announcements, security alerts, info@/noreply@ senders. One-click unsubscribe is a near-certain marker.
company_automated.not_for: A human's reply, even a templated one.

person_for_company.covers: A real person writing on behalf of a business: support agent reply, sales rep's 1:1 outreach, founder update. Often light HTML plus an unsubscribe link because it went through HubSpot or similar — the formatting is the tell, not the voice.
person_for_company.not_for: Fully automated mail with no human author.

person_private.covers: An individual writing personally: friend, colleague, family, a real 1:1 conversation. Usually plain text, no unsubscribe link. Free providers (gmail, icloud, outlook, hotmail, yahoo, aol) lean this way — but a custom domain does not rule it out.
person_private.not_for: Anything sent through a marketing or sales platform, even if signed by a person.

sender_type.instructions: Who wrote and sent `email`? Consider `email.from`, `email.was_html`, `email.has_unsubscribe_link`, and `email.one_click_unsubscribe` together — no single field decides this.

criteria.bills: Correspondence about a bill: due, paid, failed, autopay — personal or business.
criteria.community_news: Community or organization news: church, school, club, HOA. Not a conversation, not selling anything.
criteria.conversation: Friends, family, or colleagues having a genuine conversation.
criteria.feature_update: New content or feature announcement: a new season launching, new features added, product news.
criteria.job_recruiting: Job-search related: recruiter outreach, job alerts, application updates.
criteria.marketing: Marketing email: newsletter, list blast, brand content with no specific offer.
criteria.sales_promo: A sales or promotional offer: deal, discount, upsell — whether or not the recipient is a customer.
criteria.security_notice: Security or account notification: password changed, login alert, terms or policy update.
criteria.support_from_me: Someone asking the recipient for help or support: a client, customer, or colleague needing something FROM them.
criteria.support_to_me: Customer support being provided TO the recipient: a reply to their ticket or request, an agent helping them.
criteria.transactional: Transactional record: receipt, order or shipping confirmation, statement, booking confirmation. Proof of something, not a pitch.

topic.instructions: What is `email` about? Pick the single best fit. Use `email.sender_relationship` when present.

criteria: No urgency: promotions, newsletters, marketing, or FYI with nothing at stake and nothing to do.

Low: informational notice about the recipient's accounts or services; worth knowing, nothing to do, nothing expiring. One-time security/verification/login codes land here: by the time the ~15-minute triage delay elapses, the recipient has already used the code or it has expired — never score them above Low.
Moderate: the recipient is expected to reply or act, but no deadline is stated or implied.
High: action required by a deadline; a payment is upcoming and not automatic; a depended-on service is degraded; an appointment needs confirmation.
Critical: money lost or at immediate risk (failed, overdue, or fraudulent payment); a device, account, service, or server is down; a security incident needs action now.
urgency.instructions: How urgent is `email` for the recipient? Score the HIGHEST level that applies, combining what is at stake (money, access, service), whether the recipient must act, and whether there is a deadline. A notice about something critical scores by its stakes even if written as a plain FYI. Use `email.dates_mentioned` and `email.received` for deadline reasoning. One-time security/verification/login codes are never urgent: email triage runs on a ~15-minute delay, so by read time the recipient has already used the code or it has expired. Score such mail Low at most.
